convertibility_reason: Uses iCustom for the Waddah Attar Trend indicator which is a custom indicator not available as a built-in MT5 indicator. The EA relies on this custom indicator's buffer values for entry/exit decisions, requiring either replication of the indicator logic in Python or access to pre-computed values.

derived_values.name: Trend direction from buffer 0 (bullish power) and buffer 1 (bearish power)
Trend strength comparison against dead zone
derived_values.used_by: Entry gate filter - signals ignored when trend power below dead zone

other_exits: Opposite signal from Waddah Attar Trend indicator triggers close of existing position before opening new one in opposite direction

custom_logic_notes: The Waddah Attar Trend indicator internally calculates the difference between two EMAs (similar to MACD) and applies a Bollinger Band-style expansion to determine trend power. The bullish power (buffer 0) and bearish power (buffer 1) are compared against a dead_zone threshold. When bullish power > 0 and > dead_zone, a long signal is generated. When bearish power > 0 and > dead_zone, a short signal is generated. The EA closes opposite positions on signal reversal before opening new ones. Signal checks are performed only once per new bar.
python_conversion_notes: The custom Waddah Attar Trend indicator must be replicated in Python. Its internal logic: (1) Calculate EMA(fast) - EMA(slow) as MACD-like line, (2) Calculate Bollinger Bands on this line with sensitivity period, (3) Trend power = (upper_band - lower_band) / 2, (4) Bullish power when MACD_line > 0, Bearish power when MACD_line < 0, (5) Dead zone threshold filters weak signals. Once the indicator is implemented, the EA logic is straightforward: check on new bar, compare trend power vs dead zone, close opposite position, open new position with fixed SL/TP.
